terms.meaning: The 1857 struggle against British rule; the British called it only a Sepoy Mutiny.
Rudyard Kipling's idea that the British had a duty to "civilise" Indians, a cover for imperialism.
A Persian word used in Urdu and Hindi as an insult for Europeans.
The 1858 promise to respect Indians' rights, customs and religion, after the Company's rule ended.

items.name: Who called it a war of independence
items.formula: V. D. Savarkar first; Pattabhi Sitaramaiah too.
items.example: Nehru: a soldiers' mutiny that quickly became a people's revolt.

items.name: Political causes
items.formula: Subsidiary Alliance and the Doctrine of Lapse cost kings their thrones; Satara, Jhansi, Oudh and others were taken.
items.example: Bahadur Shah II was reduced to a king in name only.

items.name: Administrative causes
items.formula: High posts were only for Europeans; English replaced Persian in the courts.
items.example: Middlemen ran much of the administration.

items.name: Economic causes
items.formula: Cottage industries died, land tax was harsh, zamindars lost income, and wealth drained away.

items.name: Social and religious causes
items.formula: Racial insults ("Dogs and Indians are prohibited"), spread of Christianity, and reforms conservatives disliked.
items.example: Railways and the telegraph were viewed with suspicion.

items.name: Military causes
items.formula: Low pay, no promotion, a ban on religious symbols.
items.example: Canning's Common Military Service Act sent soldiers anywhere.

items.name: Immediate cause
items.formula: The Enfield Rifle's cartridges, which had to be bitten open, were said to be greased with pig and cow fat.
items.example: This hurt both Hindu and Muslim soldiers.

items.name: How the revolt began
items.formula: Mangal Pandey killed a British officer at Barackpore; the revolt began at Meerut on 10 May 1857.
items.example: Soldiers marched to Delhi and declared Bahadur Shah II Emperor.

items.name: Leaders and their centres
items.formula: Delhi: Bakht Khan. Kanpur: Nana Saheb, Tatya Tope. Lucknow: Begum Hazrat Mahal. Jhansi: Laxmibai. Bihar: Kunwar Singh.

items.name: The revolt in Karnataka
items.formula: Mundargi Bhima Rao, the Halagali hunters, Venkatappa Nayaka of Surapura and Baba Saheb of Nargund.
items.example: It also spread to other southern regions.

items.name: Results of the revolt
items.formula: The East India Company's rule ended and the British Queen took over India.
items.example: It inspired the later freedom movement.

mistakes.text: Mangal Pandey acted at Barackpore before the revolt; the revolt itself began at Meerut.
"White Man's Burden" was Kipling's phrase, used by the British, not an Indian idea.
The revolt failed, but it still ended Company rule.
